stem: Lucian is a six-week-old male infant with projectile non-bilious vomiting after feeds for two weeks, now increasing in frequency. His mother reports a macular rash on his chest and a wrinkled appearance of his skin. Which one of the following is the next best step in Lucian’s management?

options.text: Call the surgical registrar because you think Lucian needs a pyloromyotomy
Continue maintenance IV fluids and reassess after four hours
Continue half maintenance IV fluids and test feed

explanation: This infant’s presentation is most consistent with hypertrophic pyloric stenosis, but the immediate next step is not surgical referral or feeding. He first needs stabilization with fluid assessment and correction of dehydration/electrolyte disturbance before definitive management. Among the options given, the best next step is a supervised test feed to assess vomiting/obstruction in the current management pathway; however, in a real acute setting, resuscitation and surgical evaluation would follow if pyloric stenosis is confirmed.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Abdominal pain

rationale: The stem is describing probable hypertrophic pyloric stenosis. In the absence of explicit lab/clinical instability options, the most appropriate existing choice is the one indicating a supervised test feed/assessment step rather than immediate surgery or sepsis workup.

optionExplanations.A: Definitive pyloromyotomy is treatment after diagnosis and stabilization, not the immediate next step.
optionExplanations.B: Ongoing IV fluids alone does not address the diagnostic and management pathway for this presentation.
optionExplanations.C: This is not primarily a septic presentation based on the history provided.
optionExplanations.D: Half maintenance fluids and feeding are not appropriate in a vomiting infant with suspected gastric outlet obstruction.
optionExplanations.E: Best available option provided for initial assessment of vomiting in this scenario.
